theater: 西域南道交河、焉耆、龜茲

battle.name: 唐太宗對西域諸國的戰爭
battle.theater: 西域南道交河、焉耆、龜茲
battle.brief: 貞觀十四年正月起，唐太宗以交河道行軍大總管侯君集率漢兵與回紇、突厥之眾西出玉門，滅麴氏高昌，置西州與安西都護府於交河；其後平焉耆、克龜茲，設都督府。交河城高十餘丈，守軍登城以弓弩拒唐軍雲梯、飛石；卡面秦弩即承守城壓制之勢，後演為唐軍擘張弩與攻城諸器同場競逐。

kit.name: 秦弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，射速遠勝拉弓。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 這場戰爭是唐太宗貞觀年間在中亞乾旱地帶拉開的一條連續戰線，交戰方是唐帝國與西域南道的高昌、焉耆、龜茲、于闐諸城邦，以及捲入其中的西突厥勢力。唐方以兵部尚書侯君集任交河道行軍大總管統軍，兵員是關中與河西抽調的禁軍、府兵為主，輔以回紇與突厥的蕃兵，帳下有牛進達、契苾何力等將領，御史臺另遣官員隨軍監察，後勤沿涼州、瓜州、敦煌一線設驛站轉輸，糧秣靠河西屯田與隨軍輜重車隊維持，戰事告一段落即在西域設立安西都護府接管地方。西域一方以高昌國為主體，麴氏王族控制交河、田地、柳中等城，國小兵弱而城牆高厚、渠道密布；焉耆、龜茲各守其土，或倚西突厥為外援，或與唐保持使節往來，其中龜茲國相那利尤其排唐，多次阻撓唐使並煽動抗拒。整個戰區是一條南北狹長的綠洲走廊，漢家的遠征補給線與西域城邦的割據傾向在此正面碰撞，誰控制天山南路的節點，誰就控制絲路中段。
countriesEn: This war was a continuous front opened by Emperor Taizong of Tang across the arid belt of Central Asia, fought between the Tang empire and the city-states of Gaochang, Yanqi, Kucha and Khotan on the southern route of the Western Regions, with the power of the Western Turks drawn into it. On the Tang side the command was given to the Minister of War Hou Junji as General of the March for the Jiaohe Route. The troops were drawn chiefly from the imperial guards and the fubing system of the central plain and of Hexi, reinforced by Uyghur and Turk contingents, with generals such as Niu Jinda and Qibi Heli under him, and the Censorate keeping a supervisory officer with the army. Logistics ran along the line of Liangzhou, Guazhou and Dunhuang, where relay stations were set up; grain was supplied by the state farms of Hexi and by the baggage train that marched with the army. When a stage of the fighting closed, the Tang established a Protectorate General to Pacify the West to take charge of the region. On the other side stood Gaochang, whose Qu royal house held Jiaohe, Tiandi and Liuzhong, a small and thinly populated kingdom whose strength lay in high walls and a dense network of irrigation channels. Yanqi and Kucha each sat on their own ground, some leaning on the Western Turks for support, some keeping embassies open with the Tang, and among them the Kucha minister Nali was especially hostile, repeatedly obstructing Tang envoys and stirring up resistance. The whole theatre was a narrow north-south corridor of oases, where the long-range supply line of the Chinese state met the separatist habits of the Western Regions city-states head-on; whoever held the nodes of the southern Tian Shan held the middle of the silk road.
people: 唐太宗李世民用人不疑，是這場戰役的總設計者。貞觀十四年正月，他任命兵部尚書侯君集為交河道行軍大總管，發兵及回紇、突厥之眾數萬西征，這就是高昌之役的開端；大軍行至柳谷，水源告罄，諸將議退，他遣使持節宣慰，賜帛千匹，逼令全軍續進，才打下田地城、直抵交河城下。侯君集主持了全部攻城作業，造雲梯、撞車、飛石諸具，圍城之後先以弩手對射封住城頭射界，再以飛石摧壞城上木構，最終破門而入，迫得高昌國王麴智盛出降，所得器械二十餘萬。西域方面，高昌國王麴文泰在唐兵壓境時發病而死，嗣位的麴智盛難敵兵威，開城迎降；焉耆國王龍突豆與龜茲國相那利各懷算計，那利排唐最力，終於在貞觀二十二年（648）被阿史那社爾率兵擒斬，社爾隨後以昆陵都護身份屯駐龜茲，主持當地軍政。文字與使節一端則有玄奘：他在貞觀二十二年護送于闐、龜茲、焉耆三國使者返國，並親上表章勸說諸國內附，代表了不必動兵也能收服城邦的另一條路。
peopleEn: Emperor Taizong of Tang, who was liberal in his use of men, was the overall architect of this campaign. In the first month of the fourteenth year of Zhenguan he appointed the Minister of War Hou Junji as General of the March for the Jiaohe Route and sent out an army of tens of thousands of Han and Uyghur and Turk soldiers to the west; this was the opening of the war against Gaochang. When the army reached Liugu its water ran out and the generals proposed a withdrawal, so the emperor sent an envoy with a tally to reassure them, gave away a thousand bolts of silk, and forced the whole army forward; only then was Tiandi taken and the road opened to the walls of Jiaohe. Hou Junji directed every stage of the siege work, having cloud ladders, battering rams and stone-throwers built, and after the investment he first used crossbowmen to exchange fire and shut down the firing arcs of the walls, then brought stone-throwers to break up the timber structures on the ramparts, and finally broke in at the gate, forcing the King of Gaochang, Qu Zhisheng, to surrender and yielding more than two hundred thousand pieces of captured equipment. On the Western Regions side the King of Gaochang, Qu Wentai, fell ill and died as the Tang army closed in, and his successor Qu Zhisheng, unable to stand against the army, opened the city and came out to surrender. The King of Yanqi, Long Tuduo, and the Kucha minister Nali each pursued their own designs, and Nali was the most determined opponent of the Tang; in the twenty-second year of Zhenguan (648) he was taken and beheaded by the troops of Ashina She'er, who then held Kucha as Kunling Protector and took charge of its administration. On the side of writing and diplomacy there was Xuanzang, who in the twenty-second year of Zhenguan escorted the envoys of Khotan, Kucha and Yanqi back to their countries and personally presented a memorial urging them to submit, standing for a route by which city-states could be won over without a battle.
kits: 卡面上的秦弩是這條戰線上最不起眼卻最吃重的裝備。弩機把拉力儲存起來，靠機牙與機弦釋放，射速遠勝拉弓，守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。戰國末到秦代，弩已是成熟兵器，湖北雲夢睡虎地秦墓出土的銅弩機可證其機關形制；唐承秦制，把弩列為制式裝備，以擘張弩最為有力，張弦需數人合力，行軍時拆為弩機、弩臂、弓弦三件攜帶，交戰時合機發矢，另備大量弩矢隨軍。攻城方的對應手段是雲梯、撞車、飛石與巢車：雲梯用以登城，撞車用以破門，飛石用以摧毀城頭林木與守軍陣位，巢車高十丈可俯瞰城內、居高放箭。弩因此在城頭與城下同時發揮作用，攻城方用弩手壓制城頭的射界，防守方用弩把接近的雲梯打成碎木。軍中另備大盾、拒馬、橫刀、長矛，騎兵用弓箭，回紇與突厥蕃兵多自備弓矢，唐軍則以弩為骨幹火力，一支隊伍中弩手與長兵的比例，決定了它在城下能撐多久。
kitsEn: The Qin crossbow shown on the card is the least conspicuous and yet the most consequential piece of equipment on this front. The trigger mechanism stores the draw, and the release is handled by the catch and the string, so the rate of fire far exceeds that of the bow, and it is the crossbow that lets a defending side pin the men climbing the walls. From the late Warring States period through the Qin the crossbow was already a mature weapon, and the bronze trigger mechanisms excavated from the Qin tombs at Shuihudi in Yunmeng, Hubei, demonstrate the form its mechanism had taken. The Tang inherited the Qin design and raised the crossbow to standard issue, with the bedded crossbow, the pulang nu, the most powerful of them, needing several men to cock the string; on the march it was carried in three pieces, the lock, the bow and the string, and assembled before the shot, with a large supply of bolts travelling with the column. The besiegers answered it with cloud ladders, battering rams, stone-throwers and siege towers: the ladder for climbing, the ram for the gate, the stones for breaking up the timber on the ramparts and the standing positions of the defenders, and the tower, ten zhang high, raised above the city so that its archers could shoot down into the streets. The crossbow therefore worked on both sides of the wall, the besiegers using their crossbowmen to dominate the firing arcs from above, the defenders using theirs to break the approaching ladders into splinters. The column also carried large shields, caltrops, sabres and long spears; the cavalry used bows, the Uyghur and Turk contingents brought their own arrows, and the Tang relied on the crossbow as its core firepower, the ratio of crossbowmen to close-in troops in each unit deciding how long it could hold its position before the walls.
tactics: 唐軍的戰法是一套典型的遠征攻城程序：先以輕騎循綠洲大道推進，宿營必就水，把水源當作補給節點；再以步卒合圍，圍而不急攻，環城築柵，斷絕城內外往來；最後集中器械一次破城。柳谷正是這套程序的險處，大軍破柳谷之後一路取地八百里而井泉皆竭，士卒飢渴，幾欲退軍，唐太宗以詔書與賜帛激之，軍心復定，兵鋒直趨交河。攻城階段，侯君集先造雲梯、撞車逼近城下，又築高台、穿地道配合，圍城中的高昌人憑城頭弓弩與飛石抵抗，唐軍以弩手對射壓制城頭，再以飛石摧其木構與通道，城防一破即按街坊分段掃清，逐段入城。佔領之後不屠城、不掠民，只收其戶口、器械與屯田冊籍，安置歸義官吏，把交河改建為西州並設安西都護府，令一次性征服變為長期駐防。往後對龜茲的戰役更見鋒利，阿史那社爾選精騎為前驅，兵臨城下即驟攻其城，旬日而破，再以郡縣與羈縻並行編制新附之地，新附諸國的兵被拆散編入唐軍序列，攻城之後的整編，與攻城本身的勝負同樣重要。
tacticsEn: The Tang method was a textbook procedure for a distant campaign and a siege. Light cavalry first pushed forward along the oasis road, always camping close to water and treating the springs as the pivot of supply; infantry then closed in, investing the city without hurrying the assault, fencing it round to cut the traffic between town and countryside, and only at the end concentrating the siege engines for a single breach. Liugu was exactly where that procedure came close to failing: after taking the place the army had covered eight hundred li before the wells and springs ran dry, the men were hungry and parched and the column nearly turned back, until the emperor's edict and the gift of silk stiffened it again and the advance resumed on Jiaohe. In the siege phase Hou Junji first built cloud ladders and battering rams close to the wall, and added raised platforms and underground passages to work with them; the besieged Gaochang resisted from the ramparts with crossbows and stones, the Tang answered with crossbowmen firing up at the wall to hold the defenders down, then shattered the timber structures and the ways along the parapet with stones, and once the defence was broken they cleared the city street by street and entered section by section. After the capture there was no slaughter and no plunder: the household registers, the equipment and the farm accounts were taken, surrendered officials were settled, Jiaohe was turned into Xizhou with a Protectorate General to Pacify the West established there, and a single conquest was converted into a permanent garrison. The later war against Kucha was sharper still: Ashina She'er chose picked cavalry as his vanguard, and the moment the army reached the city he struck it with all speed, breaking it within ten days, after which counties and the jimi system were used together to administer the new territory, the troops of the submitted states were broken up and absorbed into the Tang order of battle, and the reorganisation after the siege mattered as much as the siege itself.
data: 可核對的數字散見於《舊唐書》《資治通鑑》與《新唐書·西域傳》。高昌交河城去京師七千餘里，按唐里折合今約三千七百公里，唐軍自長安出玉門關即須數月行程。兵數記為「率兵及回紇、突厥之眾數萬」，其中漢兵為主，回紇與突厥蕃兵為輔。柳谷破城之後連取之地達八百里而井泉皆竭，說明這條補給線的極限在哪裡。圍城之後所得，計城二十二座、戶八千四十六，器械二十餘萬。交河故城遺址今存，夯土城垣周長約六公里，城內可見佛寺、官署與渠道遺跡，與史籍所載的城郭規模相合。648年龜茲之役，唐軍以數千精騎長驅至城下，旬日而破一國，而龜茲、焉耆、于闐三國的城防在先後十年裡相繼崩解或歸附。整體的折損數字在傳世文獻中並不完整，能確證的是遠征隊伍在缺水、缺糧路段出現大量疲病，這才是此役最吃重的內部消耗。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked are scattered across the Old Book of Tang, the Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance and the New Book of Tang, chapter on the Western Regions. The city of Jiaohe in Gaochang lay more than seven thousand li from the capital, which on the Tang li works out to roughly three thousand seven hundred kilometres today, and the army needed months of marching from Chang'an out through the Yumen Pass. The strength is recorded as tens of thousands of men, Han soldiers forming the core with Uyghur and Turk contingents in support. After the fall of Liugu the column had covered eight hundred li before its wells and springs ran dry, which shows exactly where the limit of this supply line lay. What the siege yielded is counted as twenty-two cities, eight thousand and forty-six households, and more than two hundred thousand pieces of equipment. The ruins of the old walled city of Jiaohe survive today, its rammed-earth enceinte about six kilometres around, with the traces of monasteries, official compounds and irrigation channels inside, matching the scale of the city recorded in the histories. In the war against Kucha in 648 the Tang army drove several thousand picked cavalry to the walls and broke a kingdom within ten days, and over the following decade the defences of Kucha, Yanqi and Khotan collapsed or submitted in turn. The overall loss figures are not complete in the surviving texts; what can be established is that the marching column suffered heavy sickness and exhaustion on the stretches where water and grain ran short, and that this was the heaviest internal cost of the campaign.
cause: 唐太宗在貞觀初年要解一道結構性的難題：西域是絲路的咽喉，而這條咽喉握在西突厥與西域城邦手中。高昌麴氏既與西突厥結盟，又拒絕向唐廷入貢，扣留西域商旅與唐朝使者，切斷安西四鎮通向內地的通道，在太宗看來是負固不賓。深一層的動因是戰略上的：西突厥在北面與鐵勒諸部相持，唐若不在天山南路立起一個漢家的軍政據點，西域各國只能倒向西突厥，邊防便無從談起。財力與兵源的準備來自貞觀初年的休養之後國力轉厚，府兵制仍保有遠征的兵源，兵糧自涼州、瓜州及河西諸郡籌措，前線屯田已有可用的基業。加之太宗用人敢於倚重侯君集、阿史那社爾這類深習蕃情、熟悉西域地理的將領，征途上的每一處水源、每一處綠洲都有人事先打點，才有了綿延近二十年的西域經營。
causeEn: In the early years of Zhenguan Emperor Taizong needed to solve a structural problem: the Western Regions were the throat of the silk road, and that throat was held by the Western Turks together with the city-states of the region. The Qu house of Gaochang had allied itself with the Western Turks, refused to pay tribute to the Tang court, detained the merchants and envoys of the west, and cut the road by which the four garrisons of Anxi fed the interior; to the emperor this was defiance on a natural stronghold. The deeper motive was strategic. The Western Turks were occupied in the north against the various Tiele peoples, and if the Tang did not set up a Chinese military and civil post on the southern side of the Tian Shan, the states of the west could only lean towards the Western Turks, and there would be no border defence worth the name. The financial and manpower preparation came from the empire's recovery after the rest of the early Zhenguan years: the fubing system still held reserves fit for a distant campaign, the grain was raised in Liangzhou, Guazhou and the other prefectures of Hexi, and the farms on the forward line already had a working base to draw on. What made it possible was also the emperor's willingness to rely on men such as Hou Junji and Ashina She'er, who knew the foreign lands and their geography, so that every spring and every oasis along the route had been marked out beforehand. Out of all this came a Western Regions policy carried on for close to twenty years.
impact: 這串戰爭的結果，是唐第一次把軍政秩序直接鋪到天山南路。交河設西州與安西都護府，是唐朝在西域第一次建立常設的漢家機構；焉耆、龜茲、于闐相繼內附，形成以安西都護府為頂點的羈縻體系，與河西的涼州、瓜州連成一線，絲路中段重新被打通。經濟上，被平定的城邦交出屯田與水利設施，漢人移民得以進入綠洲耕作，渠堰與農具的技術隨之西傳；宗教上，佛寺的香火與僧侶往來在交河與龜茲更形密集，玄奘的取經路與唐使的路線高度重疊，西域與中亞的知識流動因此更為頻繁。戰略層面則出現轉折：西突厥在唐軍壓力下節節後退，而吐蕃趁勢向西域擴張，兩強在四鎮地區的角力一直延續到唐末，歸屬反覆易手，成為中亞地緣變化的根源之一。對唐室本身，這些遠征也暴露了長距離投放兵力與維持糧道的代價，遠征雖勝而兵疲，成為貞觀末年調整西域政策的背景。
impactEn: The outcome of this series of wars was that the Tang for the first time laid its own military and civil order directly across the southern route of the Tian Shan. The establishment of Xizhou and of the Protectorate General to Pacify the West at Jiaohe was the first permanent Chinese institution in the Western Regions. Yanqi, Kucha and Khotan submitted in turn, producing a jimi system with the protectorate at its apex, linked in one line with Liangzhou and Guazhou on the Hexi side, and the middle stretch of the silk road was opened again. Economically, the subdued states handed over their farms and waterworks, Han settlers moved into the oases to cultivate them, and the techniques of channels and ploughs travelled west with the colonists. Religiously, the burning of the temples and the movement of monks grew denser at Jiaohe and Kucha, the route of Xuanzang's pilgrimage overlapped heavily with that of the Tang envoys, and the flow of knowledge between the Western Regions and Central Asia became more frequent. Strategically a turn came: the Western Turks fell back step by step under Tang pressure while the Tibetans expanded westward into the region, and the rivalry of the two powers over the four garrisons ran on into the end of the Tang, with the ownership of the region changing hands again and again and becoming one of the roots of the later geopolitics of Central Asia. For the Tang court itself these expeditions also showed the cost of projecting troops over such distances and keeping a supply line alive; the victories were real but the armies came home worn out, and that became part of the background to the adjustment of western policy in the last years of Zhenguan.
result: 高昌國亡，麴氏王族退出交河，唐得其城二十二座、戶八千四十六，設西州，置安西都護府；焉耆在侯君集的兵威之下重新稱臣，龜茲在阿史那社爾手下平定，國相那利伏誅，唐以郡縣與羈縻並行安置新附，于闐亦遣使內附。天山南路自此歸入唐的宗主體系，唐太宗藉此在西北邊界建立了可屯可守的縱深，絲路中段重開。軍事上的代價同樣高昂：遠征隊伍因缺水、缺糧與疲病而銳減，攻城所得的器械再多，也不能抵銷士卒與馬匹的折耗；回紇與突厥的援軍雖在，畢竟是外力，一旦唐軍主力撤回，分散的西域城邦未必守得住既得秩序。整體而言，此役是唐經營西域的開端而非終局：制度的骨架已經立下，遠征的消耗與西域諸國的反覆也同時埋下，日後安西四鎮的經營、與西突厥及吐蕃的拉鋸，以及唐末西域歸屬的混亂，都從這一串戰爭引出線索。
resultEn: The kingdom of Gaochang was destroyed, the Qu house was driven out of Jiaohe, and the Tang took its twenty-two cities and eight thousand and forty-six households, established Xizhou and set up the Protectorate General to Pacify the West. Yanqi returned to obedience under the weight of Hou Junji's army, Kucha was pacified under Ashina She'er and the minister Nali was executed, the Tang settled the new territory with counties and the jimi system together, and Khotan too sent envoys to submit. The southern route of the Tian Shan thus came under the Tang suzerainty, and Taizong gained on the northwestern frontier a depth that could be garrisoned and farmed, with the middle of the silk road open once more. The military cost was equally high. The marching column thinned out through thirst, short rations and sickness, and no quantity of captured siege equipment could make up for the loss of men and horses. The Uyghur and Turk auxiliaries were there, but they were an external force; once the main body of the Tang army withdrew, the scattered states of the west could not be relied on to hold the order they had gained. Taken as a whole, this was the beginning of the Tang Western Regions policy rather than its end. The frame of the institutions was set up, but the cost of the expeditions and the resistance of the western states were buried with it, and from this string of wars came the later line of the four garrisons of Anxi, the repeated struggles with the Western Turks and the Tibetans, and the confusion over who held the Western Regions when the Tang finally fell.
